info.title: The Stacks API v1
info.description: A single, continuously-evolving REST surface: additive changes (new fields, new optional params, new endpoints) ship without a version bump; breaking changes are a v2 conversation. See `/api/v0` for the frozen, pre-versioning API.

isOrgAdmin.description: Whether the admin routes scope the caller to the organizations they administer: an ACTIVE user with a current ADMIN membership in at least one. False for site admins, whose access is unscoped.

scope.description: The scope the audit was started with: `all` when started by a site admin, covering every publication, or `administered-orgs` when started by an org admin, covering the orgs they administered at the start. A site admin reading the audit gets that recorded scope with every result. An org admin always gets `administered-orgs`, with results further limited to the orgs they administer now.

allOf.description: Null when the latest published version has no DOI of its own.

found.description: False when DataCite has no record for the DOI. In an audit, a publication DataCite couldn't be queried for is listed under `failures` instead.

orgName.description: The publication's primary org, the one with the lowest priority.

stacksMetadata.description: Every attribute The Stacks would send DataCite.

post.description: Creates a new publication and its first (draft) version. DOI minting is deferred: it depends on the org the publication is attached to, which isn't known yet at creation time — see `PATCH .../id/{id}/draft` (`orgs`) and `POST .../id/{id}/doi`.

slug.description: Slug for the publication's access URL. Generated from the title when omitted.

importDocument.description: The document the draft comes from, stored with it. In an authoritative format (`mystmd`, a standard MyST document) the draft's fields come from the document: its frontmatter `title`, `subtitle`, `abstract`, `license` (an SPDX ID), `keywords` (stored as tags), `doi` and `authors` (found by ORCID iD, then email), the rest is the body, and none of `title`, `subtitle`, `abstract`, `body`, `doi`, `license`, `tags`, `contributors` may be sent. Without a frontmatter `title`, a leading H1 is the title. A `doi` another publication already has is left out with a warning. Nobody else is added to the byline, so a draft whose authors aren't Stacks users can't be published until someone is. Any other format is stored as is.

delete.description: Deletes a publication. One that was never published is removed permanently, along with its versions and slug, after its draft DOIs are deleted at DataCite; if DataCite fails, the publication is kept and the request can be retried. One that was published is marked as deleted: its DOIs move from findable to registered, and if it has a DOI its last published version stays reachable so the DOI keeps resolving. Publishing a new version makes it findable again.

get.description: Viewable by a contributor, a site admin, or (once the publication has at least one org attached) any member of one of those orgs — broader than the edit permission `PATCH .../id/{id}/draft` requires. With `Accept: text/markdown; variant=myst`, the draft comes back as a MyST document built from its current fields (`title`, `subtitle`, `abstract`, `license` as an SPDX ID, `keywords` from the tags, `doi`, then the body), which `PUT .../id/{id}/draft/content` accepts back unchanged. JSON stays the default; plain `text/markdown` isn't offered. With `Accept: application/vnd.thestacks.mdast+json; schema=1; version=3`, a MyST version comes back as its MyST AST, for rendering. `schema` and `version` are optional (default: the latest) and must come before any `q`; an older `version` is migrated down, a newer one gets the latest. The AST is only sent when its type is named explicitly and preferred over the other types offered. Its `ETag` is for `If-None-Match`, not `If-Match`. The draft's AST carries `messages` and is private.

patch.description: Applies a partial update to a publication's draft version, identified by publication ID. Unlike PUT, this is a true partial update: fields omitted from the body are left untouched, while fields explicitly set to `null` or `""` are cleared. Fields that fail validation are rejected individually (see `rejected` in the response) rather than failing the whole request, so the rest of the patch is still applied. The response also reports overall publish-readiness validation errors, even when the patch itself succeeds.

put.description: Replaces the draft with a MyST document, creating the draft if none is open. Its frontmatter `title`, `subtitle`, `abstract` and the body replace the draft's; `keywords` replace the tags. `license` and `doi` are only changed when given: a published publication keeps its license, and a DOI is only recorded on a never-published publication that has none, and only if no other publication has it. `authors` who are Stacks users are added to the end of the byline; nobody else is, so a draft without them can't be published until someone is. With `If-Match`, the write only happens if the draft still has that ETag; without it, the draft is overwritten unconditionally.

get.summary: Get a publication version by ID
get.description: Returns the given version of a publication, identified by id, if the caller has access to it (published versions are public; draft versions require view/edit permission). A deleted publication that once had a DOI-bearing version always returns that last published version instead, regardless of the version requested, so the DOI keeps resolving. Responds with JSON by default; append `.md` or `.json` to `versionNumber` (e.g. `v3.md`) or send `Accept: text/markdown` for a clean Markdown rendering intended for AI agents/crawlers. An explicit suffix always wins over the `Accept` header. With `Accept: application/vnd.thestacks.mdast+json; schema=1; version=3`, a MyST version comes back as its MyST AST, for rendering. `schema` and `version` are optional (default: the latest) and must come before any `q`; an older `version` is migrated down, a newer one gets the latest. The AST is only sent when its type is named explicitly and preferred over the other types offered. Its `ETag` is for `If-None-Match`, not `If-Match`. A draft version's AST carries `messages` and is private.

post.description: Converts the document at `source` and creates a draft publication from the result, owned by the caller. `format` defaults to `auto`, which picks the format from the source. Only Google Docs URLs are supported so far. With `target: { type: "draft", publicationId }` the document is re-imported into that publication's draft instead (see `DraftImportTarget`). Media in the document is copied to Raven in the background; follow its progress with `GET /imports/{importId}`.

201.description: The draft publication was created, or the target draft was re-imported.

400.description: The source isn't a supported document.

403.description: The caller can't create publications (or edit the target publication), or the source document isn't accessible to Raven (e.g. a private document).

404.description: The source document doesn't exist, or the target publication or its draft doesn't (including a draft published or deleted while the document was being converted).

409.description: The target draft's media from an earlier import is still being copied to Raven. Retry once `GET /imports/{importId}` for that import reports `settled`.

422.description: The request's path parameters, query, headers, cookies, or body failed validation.

502.description: The source couldn't be fetched or read, e.g. its server returned an error or rate-limited Raven. Retrying later may work.
